text: A second case study — Caldwell & Finch Insurance, a fictional company used purely as a realistic scenario. This time the problem spans three separate systems, not one pipeline.

Customers got the same renewal email two or three times, and a customer-count metric kept creeping up with no real growth. The CRM, the policy system, and the support system each create their own customer record, keyed differently. A downstream 'unified customer view' merges them by email address — but slightly different formatting for the same person creates duplicate rows.

Tracing upstream and downstream shows the unified view feeds four consumers: the marketing send list, the leadership customer count, a churn calculation, and a compliance report. All four were quietly wrong in the same direction, which is why the count crept up even without real growth.

The formatting fix closes the immediate gap, but the real problem was structural: no system was ever designated the authoritative source of record for the customer identifier. The lasting fix assigns the CRM's ID as authoritative, requires the other systems to capture it, and documents the cross-system lineage explicitly.
Next up: a hands-on practice lab — you'll trace a lineage path through a small, fictional system yourself, on paper, no software required.
